description:
JSONPlaceholder is a *fake* API: it accepts almost anything and answers 201 without validating.
  These scenarios therefore pin the part of the expected outcome that is true of the live service - it must never
  fail server-side (no 5xx), must answer with well-formed JSON, and must not corrupt the data it echoes back.
  The strict reading ("invalid input must be rejected with 4xx") is kept as @known-gap scenarios, run on demand
  with `npm run test:gap`, so the deviation is documented with evidence instead of hidden.

elements.name: Control - a valid post is created

steps.name: I create a post using the "valid" payload
the response status is 201
the response body echoes the "valid" payload and adds an id

elements.name: Excessively long title (title-1k) never causes a server error

steps.name: I create a post using the "title-1k" payload
the API does not fail with a server error
the API answers with a controlled status of 201, 400, 413 or 422
a JSON body is returned when the request was accepted
an accepted title is echoed back without truncation or corruption
